scope: All 167 catalogue previews, including stations and display objects; visual review and model-definition audit, not implementation.

method.gif_source: Existing docs/ships GIFs, each exported by the actual Display.shipPortrait renderer. All 167 manifest inputs matched current TOML and renderer fingerprints at audit start.
method.visual_review: Viewed all six contact sheets at renderer frames 0,8,16; compared repeated outlines and broken family relationships.
method.quantitative_support: Six views per ship (frames 0,4,8,12,16,20). Cyan hull masks cropped to remove labels, centred and uniformly scaled preserving projected aspect ratio. Mean silhouette intersection-over-union ranks candidates. Not a claim of historical accuracy or a standalone rejection test.
limitations: Reduced 256px portraits and masks omit fine details; inspect larger renders and source images before remodeling source-backed hulls.
Camera rotation samples are the renderer animation, not orthographic engineering plans.
All imported meshes were visually reviewed, but source-backed does not mean every silhouette has been authenticated against every Elite edition.
Snapshot hashes permit checking whether later Elite Coder edits supersede this audit.

family_relationship_checks.finding: User explicitly says Mk II, Custom and Scout look nothing like an Asp. Re-anchor the base silhouette to recognisable Asp reference geometry, then create variants. Merely making three invented hulls similar is insufficient; current imported Mk II must also be reviewed, not assumed acceptable.
Mk II uses a broad generic wedge unlike the elongated Anaconda. Preserve a recognisable lineage while distinguishing the upgrade.
IV/V use unrelated generic recipes instead of a source-informed Cobra evolution. Verify each edition; the Cobra I is legitimately a different predecessor.
Python Mk II is a generic needle/stabiliser design unrelated to the recognisable Python hull.
Explorer and Scout use entirely different generic wedge forms instead of a consistent Diamondback architecture.
Generated Mk II/III/IV are generic fighters also used by unrelated craft. Check original/Frontier/modern edition relationships, avoiding automatic one-shape treatment across all versions.
Imperial Eagle uses the generic modern fighter template, not a source-informed Eagle variant. Historic Eagle I/II/III are imported renditions; do not overwrite those solely to match a modern variant.
Attack Fighter is a generic fighter while X has recognisable source geometry. Verify the correct edition-specific relationship.
Mk II is the same generic freighter seen in Hauler/Type craft; verify Elite-A identity rather than presume a same-name modern variant.
Modern Mk II is a generic freighter unlike the sourced historic Panther. Verify modern references and intended evolution; do not force identical historical/modern hulls.
Family similarity exists but comes from a shared generic freighter pattern also used elsewhere. Verify Frontier/FFE specifics.
Beluga/Dolphin/Orca are near-identical generic pods. Preserve manufacturer style but give each its reference silhouette.

All 12 use the same petals algorithm with ID-dependent petal counts. Interceptors, scouts, hunters and Titan must be checked as distinct design classes; a scaled flower is not sufficient. Shared alien aesthetic is intentional.

source_backed_and_legitimate_similarity_.finding: Imported Hydra I/II resemble each other; existing source mapping deliberately shares a hydra base. Check source-defined differences, not arbitrary visual separation.
Ionics Redback/Whitetail have closely related imported geometry. Check original pack lineage before treating similarity as a defect.
Coriolis/Dodo/Rock Hermit all appear approximately round in reduced silhouettes but geometry and roles are distinct; shape metrics over-score this legitimate similarity.
Puma/Arafura have high small-image overlap but source meshes and surface detail differ; require a larger source/reference comparison before any rewrite.
Fer-de-Lance/Black Widow have similar sourced outlines; check expansion lineage rather than replace source geometry because of a score.

implementation_priorities: Fix the user-rejected Asp family first, using actual Asp reference silhouettes including the base Mk II.
Replace generic shapes shared by unrelated hull families; the visual requirement is recognisable identities, not different vertex hashes.
Review all 93 authored interpretations, not only the original 19 user examples. Preserve credible source geometry and verify related variants.
Use actual reference views for each edition before authoring. Do not invent arbitrary extra fins or random asymmetry to pass similarity tests.
Produce source-informed before/after game-rendered comparison sheets; re-audit family resemblance and cross-family collisions.
Keep gameplay, prices, cargo, loadout and ownership stable during visual rework. Preserve licensing when deriving imported geometry.
Update authoritative TOMLs and maintained authoring paths consistently; run focused checks and make ci for implementation. README media only via make readme-media.
